title: Palworld Regions Roadmap | From Windswept Hills To The World Tree | Palworld Guide
description: A Palworld 1.0 roadmap of the map: starting in Windswept Hills, the mid game regions, how Feybreak unlocks Sunreach, and what you need to reach the World Tree.

sections.heading: The whole map in one trip
sections.script: Palworld has grown into a huge map. Version one point zero added Sakurajima, Feybreak, Sunreach and the World Tree, so where you go next can feel confusing. In this guide we walk through the regions in the order most players visit them, with rough level ranges, the gates between them, and what to prepare. A note before we begin. Guides give slightly different level ranges, so we will use approximate numbers that sources agree on, and you should trust the in game recommendations over any list. Ready to explore? We will go region by region, from the safe starting hills to the final tree, and tell you what each stop is good for. Let us start where every run begins.

sections.heading: Windswept Hills, the start
sections.script: Every run starts around the Windswept Hills. Two guides place it at roughly level one to fifteen, which makes it the safest zone on the map. It is the place to build your first base, catch your first Pals and learn the basics. The nearby small islands, such as Marsh Island and the Sea Breeze Archipelago, are also listed at early levels in one guide. Catching several of each common species here also gives you early experience. The first tower boss also lives in the hills, and it is a fair test of your first team. Stay here until your Pals feel solid, and do not rush ahead. Use this time to learn how work Pals handle jobs at your base, how catching works, and how to craft your first gear. A strong start makes every later region easier, because you will have more technology points, better spheres and a team that already knows how to fight.

sections.heading: The early wilds
sections.script: After the hills, the map opens into regions meant for roughly levels fifteen to thirty. A level guide lists places such as the Bamboo Groves, the Frostbound Mountains, the Moonless Shore and Verdant Brook in this range. This is where you get your first mount, which makes travel much faster. We covered mounts in another guide, and Direhowl is the usual pick. It is also the time to set up a better base, and to use fast travel points. Unlocking one gives a technology point, according to two guides, so activate them as you go. The goal here is to grow your team and your tech, because the next zones are much tougher. Fight the second and third tower bosses when you feel ready, and catch every new species you meet, since the Capture Bonus keeps your level climbing. A base near good resources will also keep your spheres, ammo and food stocked for the long trips ahead.

sections.heading: Volcano, desert and snow
sections.script: Next come the dangerous regions. Mount Obsidian, the volcano, is listed in the thirties and forties by one guide and a little higher by another, so think of it as a mid game zone. The Desiccated Dunes, a desert, and the Astral Mountains, a snowy range, sit in a similar band, roughly the forties and low fifties. Guides agree that these zones are tough and that you should arrive with strong Pals and good gear. A level guide also recommends heat resistant armor for the volcano and the desert, and cold resistant armor for the snow. Treat that as a hint to check each zone's temperature. These regions also hold ore, sulfur and some of the best Alpha Pals. Plan short trips, fast travel back to your base to restock, and bring food and healing items. Do not try to do the whole region at once. Pick a goal, such as one Alpha or one dungeon, finish it, and return.

sections.heading: Sakurajima
sections.script: Sakurajima is a cherry blossom island, added in version one point zero. One level guide places it at about fifty to fifty five, which fits the middle of the tower boss ladder, where Saya and Selyne wait at level fifty five. It adds new Pals, new settlements and new dungeons. Keengamer lists Sakurajima among the new settlements, and it also appears on the fifty to sixty five stage of one leveling route. Sakurajima is a good place to earn experience, since it holds new species for the Capture Bonus. Bring your best fighters and a few extra spheres for the new Pals you meet.

sections.heading: Feybreak, the gate
sections.script: Feybreak is a large island in the far southwest, and it is a major gate in the story. Guides place it in the fifties and early sixties. It has its own tower with Bjorn and Bastigor at level sixty, according to two guides, and beating that tower is what opens the way to the next area. Guides agree that Feybreak is the gate to Sunreach. It also has new dungeons, added in the same update. Expect strong enemies and new loot. Take your time, because rushing into a high level area with an under leveled team is the fastest way to lose progress. Catch new species, build up your party, and then go for the tower. This is a good place to level your team toward the high sixties before moving on, and a good time to raise your Pals with the tips from our leveling guide.

sections.heading: Sunreach in the sky
sections.script: Sunreach is a set of floating sky islands, added in version one point zero. Level guides place it in the sixties, roughly from the late fifties to about sixty eight. Two guides say you reach it only after the Feybreak tower, through a portal there, and one adds that the route will not appear on the map until you clear it. A glider may also be needed to cross, one guide says. At the end of Sunreach stand Auri and Shaolong, the next tower boss, at level sixty eight. Bring your best team and plenty of healing items. Sunreach is a late game area, so make sure your Pals are close to level sixty before you go. Take time to explore the islands, catch new species, and enjoy the view from above.

sections.heading: The World Tree
sections.script: The final region is the World Tree, the story finale, listed at about levels seventy to eighty. Two guides explain the gate. You need to clear the tower boss ladder and defeat Panthalus, a huge whale Pal, as part of a quest. After that the World Tree opens, with the final tower boss waiting at level eighty. One guide notes that hard mode scales these bosses up a lot. Be ready with your best Pals, the right sphere tier, and a full stock of healing items.

sections.heading: Your progression tips
sections.script: Here are the rules of thumb. Do not feel forced to fight every tower, since one guide says there is no hard requirement to fight any of them, though the usual order is the smoothest path. Spend technology points early on the structures that make you stronger. Keep a level guide open, but trust the in game recommendation. Take on a region when your team is near its level range. Bring spheres, food and healing items on every trip, and set a fast travel point as soon as you can reach one, so you can return to base quickly. And explore with a mount, because travel time adds up. The map is big, so give yourself time. Which region is your favorite so far, and which one is giving you trouble?
